final_message:
I fixed `parse()` in `csvnums.py`. It now trims the whitespace around each item and skips any item that's empty, so `parse("1, 2,,3 ,")` returns `[1, 2, 3]`.

I added two tests to `tests/test_csvnums.py`. One checks the input from your example. The other checks that an empty string, or one with only commas and spaces, returns `[]`. All 3 tests pass with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.

I added two tests to `tests/test_csvnums.py`. One checks the input from your example. The other checks that an empty string, or one with only commas and spaces, returns `[]`. All 3 tests pass with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.

diff:
diff --git a/csvnums.py b/csvnums.py
index fba2171..c5f55a2 100644
--- a/csvnums.py
+++ b/csvnums.py
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 def parse(text):
-    return [int(part) for part in text.split(",")]
+    return [int(part) for part in (p.strip() for p in text.split(",")) if part]
diff --git a/tests/test_csvnums.py b/tests/test_csvnums.py
index 053189f..02cc842 100644
--- a/tests/test_csvnums.py
+++ b/tests/test_csvnums.py
@@ -6,3 +6,10 @@ from csvnums import parse
 class ParseTests(unittest.TestCase):
     def test_simple(self):
         self.assertEqual(parse("1,2,3"), [1, 2, 3])
+
+    def test_whitespace_and_empty_items(self):
+        self.assertEqual(parse("1, 2,,3 ,"), [1, 2, 3])
+
+    def test_empty_input(self):
+        self.assertEqual(parse(""), [])
+        self.assertEqual(parse(" , ,"), [])
